name: South Dakota
covers_nil_agents: Yes. The act covers endorsement contracts (SDCL 59-10-2). The Board of Regents NIL policy also says NIL agents must be registered with the state.
summary: Register with the Secretary of State. $100, about 2 years.
contract_warning:
Warning to student-athlete
If you sign this contract:
(1) You may lose your eligibility to compete as a student-athlete in your sport;
(2) If you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into this contract, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director; and
(3) You may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.

steps.text: Fill out the Athlete Agent Registration form

steps.detail: $50 if based on another state's registration.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the state's warning in bold capital letters next to the athlete's signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words in the warning box.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete must tell them too.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel in writing within 14 days
steps.detail: They can't give up this right. If they cancel, they owe you nothing.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law (SDCL 59-10-14) and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of clients, every contract, and what you spent recruiting each athlete.

steps.text: Never give false info or anything of value to get an athlete to sign
steps.detail: Don't contact athletes until you're registered. Federal law (SPARTA) has the same kind of rules.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: SDCL 59-10-6 says the Secretary of the Department of Labor and Regulation issues registrations, but the Secretary of State's page takes the form and fees. Ask the Secretary of State which office files it.
The Secretary of State's athlete agent page lists no phone number. Get one from sdsos.gov/contacts.
